{{Short description|Finnish philosopher (born 1953)}}
{{BLP sources|date=November 2013}}
[[File:Esa Saarinen at Aalto University in Otaniemi, Espoo (January 2020, 2).jpg|thumb|right|Esa Saarinen giving a lecture at the [[Aalto University]] in January 2020]]
'''Esa Jouni Olavi Saarinen''' (born 27 July 1953 in [[Hyvinkää]], [[Finland]]) is a Finnish [[philosophy|philosopher]] who was a professor of [[applied philosophy]] at [[Aalto University]] and co-director of the Systems Intelligence Research Group,<ref name="KKO">''Kuka kukin on 2003'', pp. 867–868. Helsinki: Otava, 2002. {{ISBN|951-1-18086-X}}</ref> until his retirement in 2021.

Saarinen completed his [[PhD]] degree in 1978 at the [[University of Helsinki]], where he has since held a docentship. His extrovert public persona – he became known as the “punk doctor” – was reflected in his lectures at the university, which drew increasingly large audiences until the late 1990s.{{citation needed|date=March 2013}} After failing to get the position of full-time professor at the Department of Philosophy at the University of Helsinki, Saarinen resigned from his lecturer position.{{citation needed|date=March 2013}} Soon afterwards he was appointed professor at Helsinki University of Technology, since then renamed Aalto University.{{citation needed|date=March 2013}}

Saarinen's philosophical interests have changed dramatically, from early writings in [[formal logic]], to concerns with [[existentialism]] and later to [[mass media|media]] philosophy. The year 1994 saw the publication of Saarinen's best-known non-academic work, [[Imagology|Imagologies]]: Media Philosophy, written jointly with American philosopher [[Mark C. Taylor (philosopher)|Mark C. Taylor]].

In addition to academic teaching, Saarinen has also continued his business as a coach for Finnish companies and organisations, promoting a doctrine of [[self-actualization]].{{citation needed|date=March 2013}}

Saarinen is married to Pipsa Pallasvesa and has two sons, Jerome and Oliver, born in 1989.<ref name="KKO" />

One of Esa Saarinen's former students is the philosopher [[Pekka Himanen]].

Esa Saarinen was stabbed with a knife by a student outside a lecture hall in March 2014. He survived without life-threatening injuries.<ref>[http://yle.fi/uutiset/thursdays_papers_professor_stabbing_icebreaker_move_and_spring-like_driving_conditions/7122566 Thursday's papers: Professor stabbing, icebreaker move and spring-like driving conditions.] [[Yleisradio]]. March 6, 2014.</ref>
